subject: Tenant-specific sliced retention & keystore erase attestation request
messages:
From: Alice Farmer <alice.farmer@biocorp.com>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Cc: olga_petrov@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-07-12T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Initial ask — tenant-level sliced retention + delete proof

Hi Marcus / Olga,

Thanks for taking this. We are in the middle of a SIG maturity assessment and need to confirm a few implementation details for tenant-scoped retention and provable deletion for regulated PII. Specifically we need:

- A short attestation that Redwood supports tenant-scoped retention windows (per-tenant TTLs) for inference and session logs, and how those are enforced (object tombstones vs hard delete).
- An example "provable delete" manifest for a single deletion event (what artifacts you provide to demonstrate deletion) — CSV or JSON is fine.
- Details on keystore handling: when a tenant requests deletion, is the tenant key rotated/destroyed? How does that interact with backups and long-term object storage?
- Scoped timeline: SLA for evidence delivery (we may need this within 10 business days).

Attached is our intake (bio_retention_qs_2026-07-12.pdf) and the SIG questionnaire section we are working against. Can you confirm the deliverables and a rough timeline? Also: our security team will need a sampling plan to validate deletes (we plan to sample 3 tenants).

Thanks — appreciate the quick turnaround.

Alice Farmer
Head of Security — BioCorp Therapeutics
security@biocorp.com
From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: Alice Farmer <alice.farmer@biocorp.com>
Cc: olga_petrov@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-07-12T11:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask — tenant-level sliced retention + delete proof

Hi Alice — thanks, good questions. Short answers up front and then a proposed deliverable list below.

Summary: Redwood supports per-tenant retention windows for session logs and inference traces. Deletes are implemented as a combination of tombstone marking and background hard-erase jobs; for objects encrypted with tenant-specific key material we also support cryptographic key retirement to make data unrecoverable. We can provide a provable-delete manifest and a small sample evidence bundle for your 3 sample tenants.

Proposed deliverables (what we'll provide within 10 business days):
- Provable-delete manifest (CSV) showing object ids, timestamps, tombstone mark time, hard-erase timestamp, and audit-trace id.
- Audit log extract for each sample tenant showing the deletion workflow (request id, operator/service id, keystore rotation event id).
- Short attestation document describing the retention enforcement mechanism, backup retention carveouts (if any), and keystore rotation policy.
- Diagram of keystore lifecycle and how rotated keys impact stored ciphertext (keystore-rotation-diagram.svg).

A couple of clarifying Qs for your team so we scope correctly:
1) When you say "keystore rotation/destroyed", do you require cryptographic destruction (HSM irrecoverable destroy) or operational key retirement (remove access and rotate keys such that new writes use a new key)?
2) For backups: do you require proof of purge from cold archives (S3 Glacier-like) or is an attestational workflow acceptable (we'd show timelines and retention config and sample purge logs).

I will loop Neha for SOC2/SIG alignment and Olga for the evidence pack. Expect the first draft evidence bundle in ~7 business days once we confirm answers to the above.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Head of Trust & Security — Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai
From: olga_petrov@redwood.ai
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-07-12T13:04:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Initial ask — tenant-level sliced retention + delete proof

Forwarding Alice's request — this needs SOC2/SIG wording alignment and a quick decision on backups. Neha — can you confirm whether an attestation + sampled purge logs will meet SIG baseline for "cryptographic destroy" expectations, or whether we need to offer HSM destroy for the three tenants?

Notes:
- Customer expects deliverables within 10 business days.
- We can produce manifest and audit log exports quickly.
- HSM irrecoverable destroy is possible but has product implications (unable to restore data for customer even for lawful reasons).

If you think attestation + sampled purge evidence is adequate, we'll proceed with that and include clear language about the limitations. If SIG requires explicit HSM destroy, we'll need legal sign-off and Ops schedule.

Olga
Olga Petrov
Senior Compliance Program Manager — Redwood Inference
olga_petrov@redwood.ai
From: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
To: Alice Farmer <alice.farmer@biocorp.com>, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Cc: olga_petrov@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-07-14T16:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask — tenant-level sliced retention + delete proof

Hi Alice — appreciate the patience. Quick answers and next steps below.

Clarifications:
- For SIG/SOC2 baseline we typically provide attestation + sampled purge evidence for customer-scoped deletion requests. That includes a provable-delete manifest, audit log extracts, and a signed attestation from Redwood's compliance team.
- Cryptographic "destroy" (HSM irrecoverable key destroy) is supported as an elevated option. For customers who require legal-proof cryptographic destruction we will coordinate a one-time HSM key destroy. This is irreversible; we require a signed letter of instruction and a change window.

What we're delivering (per Marcus' outline) within 8 business days:
1) Provable-delete manifest (provable-delete-manifest.csv) for your three requested tenants. Each row will include: tenant_id, object_id, original_creation_ts, tombstone_ts, hard_erase_ts, audit_trace_id, operator_id.
2) Audit log extracts (redacted PII) showing the deletion workflow and background hard-erase job runs.
3) A short attestation doc signed by Redwood Compliance describing retention enforcement, backup carveouts, and keystore lifecycle policy.
4) Keystore lifecycle diagram (keystore-rotation-diagram.svg) and a short note about how key retirement renders ciphertext unusable (but we will call this "operational key retirement" unless you request HSM destroy).

Delivery and linkage: we will upload the evidence bundle to a secure share and send a DocuSign attestation for signature. Links: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-evidence-folder/BioCorp-2026 and https://redwood.app/portal/evidence/BIO-123.

If you need HSM-level destroy for any of the three sample tenants, please reply to this thread with (a) tenant ids and (b) confirmation that BioCorp accepts irreversible destruction. We'll then provide a schedule and required authorization form.

Next steps: Marcus/Olga will assemble the bundle and cc you when the 1st draft is ready. If BioCorp's sampling plan changes (more than 3 tenants) flag here and we'll adjust timeline.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Director, Compliance — Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
